insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution; this protocol settles verified purchase confirmation at roughly $0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost delta that isn't a pricing negotiation, it's a different category of evidence.

Each verified receipt is a cryptographically signed conversion event — no lookback window, no modeled assist, no pixel dependency. For brands auditing post-cookie attribution gaps, this is the structural alternative, not a workaround.

insights.topic: Online marketplace entry signals category expansion
insights.insight: Etsy entering the top brand list on 2026-03-30 marks the first digital-native marketplace in the dataset, confirming the protocol has moved beyond physical retail into purchase confirmation emails — the natural expansion path for DKIM-verified commerce data.

6,792 verified receipts across 14 CBSAs and growing brand diversity creates a signal asset that cannot be replicated without rebuilding the network from scratch; early brand participants extract more signal per dollar than entrants who wait.

A single cycle added 19 new CBSAs including Chicago, Philadelphia, and San Francisco before returning to quiet — marketers running geo-targeted campaigns should note that coverage is expanding in bursts, not linearly, which affects when regional signal density becomes actionable.

insights.topic: Growth acceleration decoupled from raw throughput
insights.insight: Velocity has stayed below 1.0x week-over-week for 11+ consecutive cycles while acceleration holds above 1.0x — the 7-day GMV window rose to $36,436 this cycle, suggesting compounding momentum that raw receipt counts alone would understate.
